items.title: EU/EEA/Swiss students: temporary right of residence by registering your address
items.title_it: Studenti UE/SEE/svizzeri: diritto di soggiorno temporaneo con la registrazione della residenza
items.summary: No visa or permit. EU/EEA/Swiss citizens may stay up to 3 months on a valid passport/ID without registering. For longer stays you register your residence in the population register at the local government, which automatically gives a 5-year temporary right of residence (renewed automatically for 5 years while your address stays registered). No proof of sufficient means is required.
steps: Within the first 3 months, submit a notice of residence to the local government (in Tartu: Küüni 5 or Tartu Welcome Centre, Ülikooli 17); a personal identification code is created at the same time if you have none
Within 1 month of registering, apply for the Estonian ID card at the Police and Border Guard Board (see ee-id-card-eu)
items.deadline: register at the latest after 3 months in Estonia
items.authority: Local government (Tartu City Government, population procedures department) and Police and Border Guard Board
items.notes: The right of residence is revoked automatically if you no longer have a valid registered address in the population register (the ID card is revoked with it).

items.title: EU/EEA/Swiss citizens: Estonian ID card (proof of right of residence)
items.title_it: Cittadini UE/SEE/svizzeri: carta d'identità estone (prova del diritto di soggiorno)

applies_to.stay_duration: more than 3 months, after registering residence

items.summary: After registering your address, apply for the Estonian ID card for EU citizens at a PBGB service office. It proves the temporary right of residence, is valid up to 5 years and is not a travel document. Standard processing: ready within 30 days of acceptance.
steps: Register residence first (you can apply for the ID card only after registration)
Book an appointment at broneering.politsei.ee (optional) and bring your identity document
Pay the state fee at the service office (cash or card) or by bank transfer
items.deadline: within 1 month of registering your residence
items.cost: € 45 state fee (2026); € 20 for people of retirement age or with moderate/severe/profound disability
items.authority: Police and Border Guard Board (Politsei- ja Piirivalveamet, PBGB)
items.notes: The 1-month deadline comes from eesti.ee and studyinestonia.ee; the PBGB fee page does not state a deadline.

items.title: Non-EU students staying up to 1 year (exchange or short degree period): long-stay D visa
items.title_it: Studenti extra-UE fino a 1 anno (scambio o periodo breve): visto D di lunga durata

applies_to.stay_duration: study period in Estonia up to 12 months (up to 3 months: D or C visa)

items.summary: Students without EU/EEA/Swiss citizenship need a visa or residence permit. For studies up to one year a D visa is enough and a temporary residence permit is not granted. Apply in person at an Estonian representation; processing can take up to 30 calendar days. You need, among others, the acceptance letter, travel medical insurance for the whole stay, bank statements of the last 3 months, a criminal record certificate (≤ 6 months old) and the state fee.
steps: Book an appointment at an Estonian representation handling D visas (or VFS Global where available)
Submit the form, photo, passport, insurance policy, acceptance letter, proof of income, criminal record certificate, family/biographical forms, travel reservation
Pay the € 120 state fee; travel only after the visa is issued
items.deadline: apply in time: processing up to 30 calendar days; can be applied up to 6 months before arrival
items.authority: Estonian foreign representations / Police and Border Guard Board
items.notes: UT strongly recommends a D visa even for visa-free nationals staying more than 90 days. A D visa allows travel in the Schengen area for up to 90 days in any 6-month period.

items.title: Non-EU degree students staying more than 1 year: temporary residence permit for study (TRP)
items.title_it: Studenti extra-UE di laurea oltre 1 anno: permesso di soggiorno temporaneo per studio
items.summary: Enter with a D visa, then apply for the TRP for study at a PBGB service office (appointment required; the university sends the invitation). You confirm legal income of at least € 880/month (2026) and a health insurance contract. The TRP is issued for the nominal study period, up to 5 years; it ends 30 days after you fall behind or interrupt studies. After it expires you may stay up to 270 days (9 months).
steps: Book an appointment at broneering.politsei.ee (procedure 'Applying for a residence permit')
Bring passport, completed forms and any extra documents; photo, signature and fingerprints are taken at the office
Pay the € 225 state fee at the end of the appointment
Decision within 90 days; the residence permit card follows within 30 more days
Register your residence within 1 month of the permit being granted
items.deadline: start the application immediately after arriving on the D visa

interpretations.hypothesis: Decision within 90 days of accepting the application (PBGB).
Decision within 2 months of accepting the application (Study in Estonia, older wording).

items.notes: The PBGB page defines the income requirement as four times the subsistence level set annually in the State Budget Act; the Student Guide gives € 880/month for 2026. The UT guide states that taking academic leave can affect the TRP.

items.title: Registering your address in the population register (EU/EEA/Swiss, Tartu)
items.title_it: Registrazione dell'indirizzo nel registro della popolazione (UE/SEE/svizzeri, Tartu)
items.summary: Submit a notice of residence to the local government. In Tartu: population procedures department at Küüni 5 (queue or online booking) or Tartu Welcome Centre, Ülikooli 17. Bring your ID document and, if you are not the owner, the tenancy contract or the owner's consent. Free of charge; the city checks the notice within 10 working days. First-time arrivals must go in person (no Estonian ID card yet for online registration).
steps: Fill in the notice of residence form (English version available on tartu.ee)
Go in person to Küüni 5 or Ülikooli 17 with passport/ID and tenancy contract or owner's consent
The personal identification code is created in the same procedure
items.authority: Tartu City Government, population procedures department (rahvastikutoimingute osakond)

interpretations.hypothesis: EU citizens must register at the latest after 3 months in Estonia (EU-citizen specific rule).
Tartu's service page sets a general deadline of 14 days after moving into a new permanent or main residence.

items.notes: Registered residence in Tartu also unlocks resident ('tartlane') bus fares. Ask the landlord before signing whether you can register at the address.

items.title: Registering your address after the residence permit (non-EU)
items.title_it: Registrazione dell'indirizzo dopo il permesso di soggiorno (extra-UE)

applies_to.stay_duration: holders of a temporary residence permit

items.summary: Holders of a residence permit must register their place of residence in the population register within one month after the permit is granted. In Tartu this is done at Küüni 5 or at Tartu Welcome Centre (Ülikooli 17) with passport, residence permit card and tenancy contract or owner's consent.
items.deadline: within 1 month of the residence permit being granted
items.authority: Tartu City Government, population procedures department
items.notes: Not registering can lead to revocation of the permit (PBGB Student Guide: actual place of residence must be in Estonia).

items.title: Estonian personal identification code (isikukood) for EU citizens
items.title_it: Codice identificativo personale estone (isikukood) per cittadini UE
items.summary: The isikukood is the number used for public services, taxes, the bus card discounts and state allowances. EU/EEA/Swiss citizens registering residence for the first time get it automatically with the notice of residence; it can also be requested on its own. Apply in person in Tartu (Küüni 5 / Tiigi 12 or Tartu Welcome Centre, Ülikooli 17); it is created immediately and free of charge.
items.authority: Tartu City Government, population procedures department

items.title: Estonian personal identification code for non-EU students
items.title_it: Codice identificativo personale estone per studenti extra-UE
items.summary: Non-EU nationals usually receive the isikukood as part of the TRP application at the PBGB, or through the registration of short-term employment. If needed earlier, it can be requested at Tartu Welcome Centre or Küüni 5 before the TRP application.
items.authority: Police and Border Guard Board / Tartu City Government
items.notes: Source is Tartu Welcome Centre (Tartu foreigners' service centre, listed as a service point on tartu.ee). UT notes the code must be in its Study Information System to apply for state allowances.

items.title: EU/EEA/Swiss students: EHIC and Estonian health insurance
items.title_it: Studenti UE/SEE/svizzeri: TEAM e assicurazione sanitaria estone
items.summary: Bring an EHIC (or provisional certificate) issued by your home insurer; it gives necessary care on the same terms as Estonian-insured people, with a co-payment of € 5 or € 20. Bachelor's/master's degree students from the EU are not covered by Tervisekassa unless employed in Estonia or holding permanent residence, so they can use the EHIC only if still covered at home; otherwise buy private insurance.
items.cost: co-payment € 5 or € 20 per visit (Tervisekassa page updated 19.09.2025)

interpretations.hypothesis: Degree students from the EU are not covered by Tervisekassa unless employed or with permanent residence (UT, Study in Estonia).

Tervisekassa covers higher-education students who are 'permanent residents of Estonia'; whether an EU citizen with a registered address and temporary right of residence counts is not stated on the page.

items.notes: EHIC is not a substitute for travel insurance (no private care, repatriation or lost property).

items.title: Non-EU students: mandatory private health insurance
items.title_it: Studenti extra-UE: assicurazione sanitaria privata obbligatoria
items.summary: Non-EU exchange students and bachelor's/master's degree students must buy private insurance. D visa: travel medical insurance for the whole visa validity. TRP: a health insurance contract covering the whole permit period (can be bought yearly and extended on time). The TRP may be revoked if insurance lapses. PhD students admitted from 2022/23 are covered by Tervisekassa.
items.deadline: for TRP holders, Study in Estonia says the contract must be arranged within two months of arrival
items.authority: Police and Border Guard Board (permit condition); Tervisekassa
items.notes: The insurance requirements for a D visa and a TRP differ. Any insurer may be chosen (Estonian insurer not required).

items.title: Estonian state health insurance when you work
items.title_it: Assicurazione sanitaria statale estone se lavori

applies_to.min_work_hours: employment contract for more than 1 month (or open-ended) with social tax paid

items.summary: Employees with a contract longer than one month, for whom the employer pays social tax, are insured by Tervisekassa after a 14-day waiting period from the start date entered in the employment register. Foreigners with a temporary basis of stay are insured only if employed and social tax is paid. Cover ends two months after the contract ends.
items.cost: paid through the employer's social tax
items.notes: For service/short contracts (law of obligations) cover depends on the minimum social tax: € 292.38/month in 2026 per Tervisekassa.

items.title: Voluntary Tervisekassa insurance contract

applies_to.residence_requirement: residence in Estonia per the population register

items.summary: People living in Estonia according to the population register who are not otherwise insured can buy voluntary health insurance from Tervisekassa via the Health Portal. The 2026 premium is € 3,264/year (€ 272 monthly instalments); cover starts one month after concluding the contract.
items.notes: UT mentions this option for students; whether it satisfies the TRP insurance condition was not checked.

items.title: Opening a bank account
items.summary: Requirements differ by bank and residency status. Banks may ask for a passport, an Estonian ID card or residence permit card if you have one, and proof of your connection to Estonia (study certificate, employment or rental contract, residence permit). Banks named: LHV, Luminor, SEB, Swedbank, Coop Pank. An IBAN from another European country may be accepted instead.
items.authority: Commercial banks (information by Tartu Welcome Centre)
items.notes: No official page on a legal right to a basic account or on fees was read.

items.title: Tartu bus card (personalised card for discounted fares)
items.title_it: Tessera bus di Tartu (personalizzata per le tariffe ridotte)
items.summary: Tartu city buses use an e-ticket system. Discounted fares require a bus card personalised with an Estonian personal identification code; resident fares require a registered address in Tartu city or Kambja, Luunja or Tartu rural municipality. There is no separate student category: discounts are age-based (youth 20–26). The card can be personalised free at Tartu Welcome Centre; a personalised bank card can also be used.
items.notes: Fares are in subsidies.json (ee-tartu-youth-fare, ee-tartu-resident-fare). Riding without a valid ticket can be fined € 40.

items.title: EU/EEA/Swiss students: working in Estonia
items.summary: No work permit is needed: EU/EEA/Swiss citizens may live and work freely. The employer registers you in the Employment Register of the Tax and Customs Board. No student-specific hour limit was found.
items.authority: Work in Estonia (Enterprise Estonia) / Tax and Customs Board

items.title: Non-EU degree students with a TRP for study: working
items.title_it: Studenti extra-UE con permesso per studio: lavorare

other: holder of a temporary residence permit for study

items.summary: TRP-for-study holders may work without a separate work permit as long as work does not interfere with studies and they stay full-time; no proof of employment needs to be sent to the PBGB. Study in Estonia lists working hours as 'not limited'. During academic leave you need a residence permit for employment to keep working. After graduation non-EU graduates may stay 9 months (270 days) to look for work.

items.title: Non-EU students on a D visa (studies up to 1 year): working
items.title_it: Studenti extra-UE con visto D (studi fino a 1 anno): lavorare

applies_to.stay_duration: up to 12 months on a D visa

items.summary: No page read states the work rule for students on an Estonian D visa. UT implies students with an Estonian visa may work if it does not interfere with studies; PBGB says short stays on a visa require the employer to register short-term employment. Check with the PBGB migration advisers before taking a job.

interpretations.hypothesis: Students on a visa may work on the same condition as TRP holders (work must not interfere with studies), as implied by UT's sentence about students with visas issued by other EU countries.
Work during a stay on a visa requires registration of short-term employment by the employer (general PBGB rule; students not mentioned).

items.title: Statutory minimum wage
items.summary: As of 1 April 2026 the minimum wage is € 946/month gross for full-time work and € 5.67/hour gross; part-time minimums are proportional. In 2025 it was € 886/month. No separate youth or student rate is given.
items.notes: Study in Estonia still shows € 820 (2024), which is outdated.
